title: THE MACHINE NOBODY WROTE DOWN
note: NSF award 2626692, made 2026-08-10 to UAF, PI Mariko Shirazi. Every verb about the award's work is FUTURE TENSE (period of performance begins 2026-08-15). lines.text: A rating plate on a village diesel generator.
The top number is stamped deep, the power this machine can make.
Everything under it is blank, because nobody ever wrote down how this machine behaves.
On August 10th the National Science Foundation put money behind that blank space, at the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
Set a battery beside it, about the same size, and N S F says the two can interact and produce sustained oscillations.
That battery exists to let the diesel switch off, which is where the fuel saving comes from.
So if the two fight each other instead of settling, the diesel keeps running and the saving never arrives.
On a big grid you'd study each machine alone, but here they are wired too close, and nobody wrote this one down.
So the battery's own inverter will put a question into the wire and learn how the diesel answers.
But a measurement is only the moment you took it, and a photograph of a running engine is out of date before it's pinned up.
You can take a new one any hour though, on hardware already on the wall.
And Alaska's utilities are ahead of the science, with a megawatt battery already shipped to the village of Saint Mary's.
The Fairbanks award is three hundred twenty five thousand dollars, and the test bed is a lab.
You'd expect a machine that learns to be called artificial intelligence, but this award only says data driven.
The work starts August 15th, two days from now.
The plate still won't say how that machine behaves. Fairbanks is finally going to ask it.
